title: Docker Build and BuildKit
subtitle: Faster, smarter and multi-platform image builds
description: BuildKit is the default builder and a different architecture from the legacy builder. Learn cache mounts, multi-platform builds, builders and declarative Bake files.
outcomes: Use cache mounts and registry cache effectively
Automate builds with docker buildx bake

modules.title: BuildKit in practice
modules.summary: The modern builder and its cache.

lessons.title: BuildKit architecture
lessons.summary: A DAG of build steps, executed concurrently, with content-addressed caching.
objectives: Describe how BuildKit differs from the legacy builder
Know when to use a custom builder

sections.title: A graph, not a straight line
sections.body:
BuildKit parses the Dockerfile into a directed acyclic graph of operations. Independent stages and steps can run in parallel. It uses content-addressed caching, supports secret and SSH mounts, and can emit provenance/SBOM data.

The **docker** driver builds inside the daemon’s image store. The **docker-container** driver runs BuildKit in a container and unlocks multi-platform builds, registry cache, and isolation from the daemon image store.

sections.code:
docker buildx version
docker buildx ls
docker buildx create --name ci-builder --driver docker-container --use
docker buildx inspect --bootstrap
docker buildx build --load -t acme/api:dev .
sections.output:
NAME/NODE       DRIVER/ENDPOINT             STATUS      BUILDKIT
default         docker                      running     v0.15
ci-builder*     docker-container            running     v0.15

sections.caption: Build context → parse → DAG → parallel execution → layers → image or cache export.

sections.title: BuildKit is the default
sections.body: Docker Engine 23.0+ uses BuildKit for `docker build` on Linux. The legacy builder is deprecated; do not build new workflows around it.

questions.explain: BuildKit builds and executes a dependency graph.

lessons.title: Cache mounts and registry cache
lessons.summary: Keep package manager caches across builds and share build cache through a registry.
objectives: Export and import cache with buildx

sections.title: Cache mounts vs layer cache
sections.body:
A layer cache stores the result of an instruction. A **cache mount** persists a directory (npm, pip, Go modules) across builds without adding it to the image layer. This keeps images small while avoiding repeated downloads.

For CI, export cache to a registry or local directory and import it in later runs with `--cache-to` and `--cache-from`.

sections.code:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm \
    npm ci --prefer-offline
COPY . .
RUN npm run build
sections.note: The npm cache is not part of the final image; it lives in BuildKit’s cache store keyed by the mount id.
mode=max caches intermediate layers, not only the final image.

sections.title: Cache can hide supply-chain changes
sections.body: A cached `apt-get install` may not see an updated package index. Use `--no-cache` for security rebuilds and pin base images by digest.

lessons.title: Multi-platform builds and Bake
lessons.summary: Build for amd64 and arm64 at once, and define repeatable build targets in a file.
objectives: Use docker buildx bake for CI

sections.title: Multi-platform output
sections.body:
Multi-platform builds require a builder that supports them (docker-container driver). BuildKit schedules a build per platform, potentially using QEMU emulation for foreign architectures. Emulation is slow; native runners are faster for large builds.

`--push` or `--load` is required because a multi-platform result is an image index, not a single image loadable into the local store.

sections.code:
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  -t registry.example.com/acme/api:1.4 \
  --push .

docker buildx imagetools inspect registry.example.com/acme/api:1.4
sections.output:
Name: registry.example.com/acme/api:1.4
MediaType: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json
Manifests:
  linux/amd64
  linux/arm64

sections.note: Run with `docker buildx bake` or select targets with `docker buildx bake api`.

sections.title: Bake is for teams
sections.body: A Bake file keeps CI and local builds identical, supports inheritance, and can build several images in parallel.

questions.question: Why can a multi-platform image not be --load-ed?
options: It is an image index with multiple manifests
questions.explain: The result is a manifest list/index; push it to a registry.

questions.question: What is QEMU used for?
questions.explain: BuildKit uses emulation when the host cannot run the target architecture natively.

questions.question: Which command runs a Bake file?
questions.explain: buildx bake is the entry point.
